register.name: Australia, earthquake humanitarian and recovery assistance
register.detail: Australian Government · after the earthquake of December 2024 · emergency medical and search and rescue teams, relief supplies, restoring critical services and infrastructure
register.note: Australia also gave over A$17.6 million after Tropical Cyclones Judy, Kevin and Lola in 2023
register.text: Humanitarian and recovery assistance from Australia after the earthquake of December 2024. It paid for emergency medical and search and rescue teams, relief supplies and support to restore critical services and infrastructure, which protect the health and shelter standards in a crisis.

register.name: Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program, first phase (Vanuatu)
register.detail: World Bank · approved 5 June 2026 · project P513248
register.note: Tuna industry, small-scale fisheries and aquaculture, and fisheries governance
register.text: World Bank financing for Vanuatu’s part of a regional ocean programme. It supports the tuna industry, value chains for small and medium-scale fisheries and aquaculture, with cold chains and fish markets, and fisheries governance, which serve the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project, financing of March 2026
register.detail: World Bank · approved 19 March 2026 · project P173278
register.note: Safer, more affordable settlements in and around Port Vila
register.text: World Bank financing to improve access to infrastructure and services in selected new and existing settlements, make them more resilient to hazards and strengthen land planning and management. The settlements project supports safer, more affordable urban development in and around Port Vila, which serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Vanuatu Resilience Development Policy Financing with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · approved 14 January 2025 · $20 million for reconstruction and response · $10 million contingent financing for a future disaster or health emergency
register.note: Budget-wide; it followed the earthquake of 17 December 2024
register.text: An IDA grant after the earthquake of December 2024: $20 million towards reconstruction and response at once, and $10 million of contingent financing for rapid access in a future disaster or health emergency. It supports reforms for fiscal stability, governance and transparency, and resilience planning under the Disaster Risk Management Act, protecting the budget behind all seven standards.

register.name: Climate Resilient Transport Project, additional financing II
register.note: A transport instrument: roads and bridges built to withstand cyclones
register.text: Roads and bridges that withstand cyclones.

register.name: Enhancing Adaptation and Community Resilience by Improving Water Security in Vanuatu (FP191)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · grant · approved 20 October 2022 (B.34) · accredited entity: Pacific Community (SPC) · effective 19 September 2023 · 34% disbursed · ends 19 September 2028
register.note: Total value $28.3 million; 303,000 people expected to gain resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, approved in 2022 and under way to 2028, to create safe, climate-resilient and sustainable water use and improve water security in local communities. It upgrades and scales up the government’s water management and builds skills in water resources management, which serves the water standard, the one furthest from reach in Vanuatu.

register.name: Vanuatu Community-based Climate Resilience Project (FP184)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · grant · approved 19 May 2022 (B.32) · accredited entity: Save the Children Australia · effective 24 October 2022 · 56% disbursed · ends 24 October 2028
register.note: Total value $32.7 million; about 200,000 people expected to gain resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, approved in 2022 and under way to 2028, for community adaptation in farming and fisheries, climate information and local early warning. It sets up local disaster risk reduction committees, protects and restores 11,600 hectares of farming and fishing sites and trains smallholders and fishers, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Greater Port Vila Urban Resilience Project, third financing
register.detail: ADB · Asian Development Fund grant · approved, announced 29 September 2026 · $5.6 million Green Climate Fund grant through the Community Resilience Partnership Program Investment Fund · $700,000 in kind from the Government
register.note: At least 23,400 people, 11,700 of them women, expected to benefit directly by 2031
register.text: An ADB grant for three multipurpose emergency shelters in Agathis, Freshwind and Nambatri, which serve as refuges in disasters and as community spaces and markets at other times, and for an emergency shelter strategy. It follows ADB grants of $9.6 million in 2020 and $2.9 million in 2022 for urban resilience in Greater Port Vila and serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Vanuatu Rapid Response Contingent Project
register.detail: ADB · approved, announced 25 August 2026 · the first project under the Rapid Resource Reprogramming and Deployment Option (3RDO)
register.note: Redirects part of Vanuatu’s undisbursed ADB financing; no new amount is stated
register.text: The first project approved under ADB’s region-wide crisis financing mechanism, which lets Vanuatu redirect part of its undisbursed ADB financing to emergency response and early recovery. The financing can support families, deliver essential supplies and equipment and repair damaged public services and infrastructure after cyclones, earthquakes, droughts or economic crises, which protects the food, shelter and health standards.

register.name: Vanuatu Sustainable Economic Transformation Facility
register.detail: ADB · Asian Development Fund grant facility · approved, announced 23 June 2026 · project 59361-001 · an initial $2.5 million for the Vanuatu Project Management Unit and the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management
register.note: ADB’s first Small Expenditure Financing Facility in the Pacific; budget-wide
register.text: Flexible, multisector grant financing to help the Government respond faster to development needs, strengthen project and financial management, procurement, safeguards and monitoring, and pay for maintenance and rapid disaster recovery. Its priority areas include public–private partnerships, digital transformation, agriculture and water security, which bear on the food and water standards.

register.name: Enduring Fiscal Position Program, subprogram 1
register.detail: ADB · Asian Development Fund · approved 2025 · $10 million policy-based grant for budget support · $10 million multiyear contingent disaster financing
register.note: Budget-wide; the World Bank gave $30 million of grant cofinancing for subprogram 1, ADB reports
register.text: ADB budget support for structural reforms after the earthquake of December 2024, with a further $10 million of contingent disaster financing that can be drawn after a disaster. It aims to make Vanuatu’s fiscal position more sustainable and protects the budget behind all seven standards.

register.name: Noncommunicable disease care in the northern provinces
register.detail: ADB · Asian Development Fund grant · committed 2025 · project 53084-001 · Malampa, Penama, Sanma and Torba
register.note: More than 150,000 people expected to benefit
register.text: An ADB grant to expand access to quality care for noncommunicable diseases across the four northern provinces, with a dedicated clinic in Luganville. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Luganville Resilient Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 2024 · grant 0966-VAN(SF), $16.02 million · loan of $41.66 million from ordinary capital resources · agreements dated 27 November 2024 · grant closing 31 March 2033
register.note: About 35,000 people on Espiritu Santo expected to benefit
register.text: ADB grant and loan financing to develop resilient water systems in Luganville on Espiritu Santo, for about 35,000 people. It serves the water standard, the one furthest from reach in Vanuatu, and the shelter standard through sanitation.

register.name: Supporting the Delivery of Skills Development Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 30 August 2024 · grant agreements signed 16 September 2024 · effective 3 December 2024 · grants 0959-VAN and 9243-VAN
register.note: Vanuatu Institute of Technology; 1,300 students a year to be supported
register.text: ADB grants to strengthen the Vanuatu Institute of Technology and expand training at two campuses, among them the Malampa campus on Malekula. The project, which began in 2025, develops new qualifications and is to support 1,300 students a year, including women and people with disabilities, which serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Pacific Disaster Resilience Program, phase 5 (Vanuatu)
register.detail: ADB · grant · approved, announced 28 June 2024 · quick-disbursing, flexible budget support after a disaster · part of a $41 million package for five Pacific nations
register.note: Budget-wide; for disasters triggered by natural hazards and health emergencies
register.text: Contingent ADB grant financing that gives Vanuatu quick-disbursing, flexible budget support after a disaster triggered by a natural hazard or a health emergency. It protects the budget behind the seven standards when a cyclone or an earthquake strikes.

register.name: Australian development assistance to Vanuatu, 2026–27
register.detail: DFAT · budget estimate 2026–27 · bilateral allocation A$50.0 million · total A$85.6 million in the 2025–26 budget estimate
register.note: Total official development assistance attributable to Vanuatu; Australia is its largest health sector partner, DFAT says
register.text: Total Australian official development assistance attributable to Vanuatu in the 2026–27 budget, of which A$50.0 million is the bilateral country programme. DFAT describes sectoral and general budget support, health, education, water and sanitation through NGO partners, and climate resilience, which bear on the seven standards.

register.name: Project for Strengthening Disaster Resilience of Health Care Facilities in Remote Islands
register.detail: Government of Japan with UNICEF · notes signed and exchanged 10 February 2026, Port Vila · grant up to ¥1.095 billion
register.note: Water, sanitation and solar power for health facilities on the outer islands
register.text: A grant from Japan, implemented with UNICEF, to install water and sanitation facilities and solar power systems at health and medical facilities on the outer islands and to train health workers in medical management. It serves the health, water and energy standards on the most remote islands, where disasters and emergencies are hardest to answer.

register.name: New Zealand International Development Cooperation with Vanuatu, 2024–27
register.detail: MFAT · approved funding for 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2027 · 2024–27 plan target NZ$150.97 million
register.note: A three-year plan target under the Pacific Development Cooperation allocation
register.text: New Zealand’s approved funding for development cooperation with Vanuatu over the three years to June 2027. Its country plan of May 2025 aims for a well-educated and trained population and better access to drinking water and sanitation resilient to climate change, with energy and health among its sectors, which bear on the education, water, energy and health standards.

items.name: VANWODs Microfinance
items.text: A women’s microfinance scheme that, with the Vanuatu Green Energy Fund and UN Women, offers concessional loans for solar systems to women living off the grid on Efate and Tanna, to power freezers, lights, sewing machines and phone chargers; 60 women had benefited by March 2025, towards a target of 100.

items.name: Aelan Chocolate Makers
items.text: A chocolate maker in Port Vila, part of ACTIV, a not-for-profit organisation that supports communities across Vanuatu through fair trade and sustainable incomes, whose shared factory makes chocolate on behalf of twelve cacao farms on different islands.
